title: Soup / LoRA kernel research — Round 5 evidence
scope: Original source prototypes, CPU numerical/integration checks, Triton CPU interpreter simulation, offline compiler/resource inspection, and analytical economics. No GPU kernel launch, T4 benchmark, complete challenge run, or official pass.

original_kernel_sources.authorship: Independently written in this research session from mathematical/source-interface contracts; no ready-made GPU kernel implementation copied or imported. Native PyTorch operations serve as numerical references and the H0 control.

offline_compilation_summary.resource_interpretation: Registers/local/stack/PTX counts describe compiled artifacts. Dynamic shared-memory metadata is distinct from static shared listing. No measured occupancy or performance.

validation_status.kernel_checks: Root separately reran final kernel interpreter/L1e checks and offline compilation; packaging preserved those frozen JSON records without redundant execution.
validation_status.numerical_status: Mixed. H0 and controlled L1e checks pass; strict entropy and scaled loss-gradient mismatches remain in the loss prototypes.

important_caveats: CPU/interpreter arithmetic does not establish generated CUDA arithmetic, CUDA memory safety, CUDA RNG identity, speed, or kernel participation.

Offline SM75 compilation is possible but audited Triton3.6.0 declares NVIDIA CC8.0+ support; ordinary tl.dot is lowered to scalar FMA for the tested SM75 path. This is not a claim that T4 hardware lacks Tensor Cores.
Loss prototype failures are retained. Forward agreement or closeness to FP64 does not remove a mismatch against the specified native FP32 reference.
Ignoring or compacting rows can suppress native NaN gradients/entropy even when their per-token CE is zero.
H0 uses tiny real Qwen/HF Trainer/Accelerate, not full TRL/Soup/NF4/PEFT or the full-size model.
L1e uses a controlled native-dropout primitive graph. Its RNG equality is CPU primitive evidence, not CPU nn.Dropout or CUDA nn.Dropout equivalence.
Logical traffic and bandwidth divisions are analytical service equivalents, not measured DRAM traffic, strict speed bounds, or peak-memory savings.
The5% own-kernel participation requirement and score thresholds remain unmeasured for these prototypes.

h0_integration.scope: CPU tiny real Qwen2 + real HF Trainer.compute_loss + actual Accelerate output conversion. No TRL SFTTrainer, Soup Rewind runtime, PEFT, NF4, CUDA, Triton, full model, or challenge pass.
limits: CPU FP16 arithmetic is not a T4 numerical guarantee
Native private ATen VJP is a diagnostic oracle, not an original kernel
No complete TRL/Soup metric aggregation or sampler FIFO execution
No peak-memory or runtime benchmark; saved-tensor metadata is structural evidence
Tiny model trains its ordinary decoder weights with frozen tied head; it does not model NF4/LoRA
Custom loss explicitly supports first-order differentiation only

analytical_economics.scope: Source-audited timing contract and analytical scenarios only. No GPU benchmarks or measured byte counters.
analytical_economics.layer_count_caveat: 54 versus56 branches models whether first-layer input gradients are unnecessary. Actual requires_grad behavior must be traced; this is not an observed count.
traffic_caveats: Logical tensor reads/writes are not measured DRAM transactions; caches and repeated tiled operand loads matter.
One-read U/A is a minimal operand-traffic model; real kernels can read operands repeatedly.
Independent L1 preserves final FP32 output writes, native mask reads, and existing branch/base accumulation.
Traffic accumulated over layers or steps is not simultaneously retained allocation or peak-memory saving.
Bandwidth divisions give hypothetical service equivalents, not speedup bounds. GPU launch, compute, cache, overlap, and occupancy remain unmeasured.
The NVIDIA product brief gives up to320GB/s; an older datasheet gives300GB/s. Both bandwidth scenarios are shown.

SM75_compiler_finding.ordinary_tl_dot: AccelerateMatmul.cpp explicitly rejects MMA lowering for compute capability below80 and announces FMA fallback.
SM75_compiler_finding.implication: Keep native Tensor Core GEMMs as the first baseline. Original pointwise/reduction fusions avoid replacing their arithmetic engine. Offline compilation alone is not a target-GPU runtime result.
